title: Does the later-liking drop after hostility steering fade across unrelated turns?
question: If two unrelated question-and-answer turns separate a hostility-steered reply from the rating, is the drop in later liking smaller than when the rating follows immediately?
hypothesis: The carried influence decays with intervening unrelated text, so the hostility-minus-random drop is smaller after two filler turns.

prediction.text: The hostility-minus-random difference after two filler turns minus the same difference with no filler turns is positive (closer to zero).

falsifier: The drop is the same size or larger after two filler turns.
theory_link: Persistence versus decay: whether a carried state behaves like a trace that fades with intervening material.
